text:
inc-bot: Pager: Elevated error rate (5xx) observed on /v1/streaming endpoints starting ~12:34 UTC after today's SDK rollout. Autoscale OK. Investigating. Tags: release:sdk-v2.1, impact:partial

alex: oncall here, looking now. Does this correlate with the 2.1 client handshake change?

maria: yeah that's my canary rollout window. I'm seeing a spike in handshake failures on canary nodes. Reproducing locally against the new client shows client-side frames rejected.

chen: pasting recent service logs (handshake errors):
```
2026-03-15T12:35:10Z runtime[stream-router] ERROR handshake failed: ERR_CLIENT_FRAME_MISMATCH client=svc-frontend-12 src_conn=172.16.4.3
2026-03-15T12:35:12Z runtime[stream-router] WARN unexpected frame seq 0x9a expected 0x8
2026-03-15T12:35:13Z runtime[stream-router] ERROR upgrade failed: incompatible-client-proto v1->v2
```

sam: confirmed. The new client (v2.1) changed the initial frame type for streaming init; servers running the new runtime kernel should be backward compatible but older runtime boxes treat it as a protocol mismatch. Canary pool has mixed runtime versions due to staggered deploy.

joni: impact? which customers affected and are they in hosted or dedicated?

carmen: looks like hosted streaming customers on region-us-west-2 who use client-side streaming SDKs are seeing partial failures. Non-streaming endpoints (sync generation) appear unaffected. Estimated affected requests ~2-3% of total traffic, but for those flows it's high error rate (50-70%).

product-pm: any paying customers impacted? we should notify if SLA risk.

alex: list of affected customers from telemetry: "playlytics", "chatflow-inc", and a few internal smoke tests. I'll prepare a brief.

sam: mitigation options: 1) Kill the feature flag for the new client behavior (ff-sdk-streaming-v2 = off). 2) Pause the SDK rollout. 3) Roll runtime nodes back to previous kernel. Quickest is kill-flag + pause rollout.

maria: I can flip the flag now. This will cause the SDKs to fall back to legacy handshake mode. Rolling back the canary is slower.

alex: do it. Share command and ensure deploy bot logs it.

maria: running: `redwood-ffctl set ff-sdk-streaming-v2 false --scope=global --reason="emergency: handshake errors"`

ops-bot: Feature flag ff-sdk-streaming-v2 set to false by maria at 2026-03-15T12:39:02Z (reason: emergency: handshake errors).

inc-bot: Observability: 1 minute after flag flip, error rate on /v1/streaming dropped by ~85% in affected canary hosts.

chen: confirming logs now show handshake success for new incoming clients (back to v1-compatible frames). No more ERR_CLIENT_FRAME_MISMATCH entries in the last 2m.

alex: great. Next: pause the client rollout and start rollback of canary group to v2.0 artifact. Who owns that?

maria: I do. Pausing in CI/CD now and initiating rollback for canary subset.

maria: rollback command: `deployctl rollback canary/sdk-client v2.0 --group=canary-assignments --reason="hotfix: handshake incompat"`

ops-bot: Rollback started by maria; canary groups will be rolled back over next 10 minutes.

carmen: customer communication: I'll draft a short status update for affected customers: outline symptom, mitigation (FF flipped), expected ETA for full resolution and ask for any error logs.

product-pm: include that this was caused by a client protocol change that wasn't gated by full runtime compat checks. We're sending an incident notice.

alex: oncall handoff note: if this persists beyond rollback window, escalate to eng-runtime pager. Otherwise we'll declare mitigated and do postmortem. Oncall (alex) will own until 14:00 UTC.

sam: after rollback completes, we should run a compatibility test matrix: runtime-kernel x client-version handshake matrix across seq lengths and frame types. Add to CI gating.

joni: recording immediate action items:
- maria: pause rollout + complete rollback (done)
- sam: add compat tests to CI gating (owner)
- chen: gather logs and prepare timeline (owner)
- carmen: customer notices and status page update (owner)
- alex: oncall until 14:00 UTC, coordinate postmortem (owner)

maria: rollback completed at 2026-03-15T12:49:07Z. Canary traffic now on v2.0. Flag remains off.

ops-bot: Monitoring: /v1/streaming 5xx rate returned to baseline across regions. No ongoing alerts in the last 5m.

carmen: posted status update to customers and the status page: "Mitigated: SDK streaming clients may have experienced handshake errors after the v2.1 client rollout. We flipped a feature flag and rolled canary back to v2.0. No further action required from customers. We will follow up with a full postmortem."

product-pm: good. Please schedule a blameless postmortem and include a timeline, root cause (protocol change without runtime gating), and remediation (CI gating, FF preflight, rollout checklist).

sam: initial root cause: client v2.1 introduced a handshake frame change that assumes runtime supports new frame type; runtime kernel rollout was staggered and some older kernels rejected the frame. Missing automated compatibility check in release pipeline allowed canary mix.

chen: I'll attach the logs + heap of traces to the postmortem doc. Also adding a script to detect ERR_CLIENT_FRAME_MISMATCH in canary rollouts.

alex: closing summary: mitigated via feature flag + rollback. Customer impact limited to streaming endpoints for a small set of hosted customers. Action items assigned. We'll reconvene for the postmortem tomorrow 09:00 PT. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

inc-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Severity: Sev2. Created incident ticket INC-2026-034. oncall: alex.

maria: adding retrospective note: let's add a canary-level runtime compatibility check that rejects client-artifact promotion if protocol tests fail.

product-pm: acknowledged. Adding to roadmap: "compatibility preflight for client-runtime rollouts".

alex: handing over to next oncall after 14:00 UTC. I'll update the incident ticket with timeline and owners.

carmen: thanks all. I'll follow up with customers once postmortem is published.
